text: A real sales organization with forty separate territories would genuinely need forty entirely separate static roles, each one manually assigned to the right people by hand. Dynamic row-level security solves that exact same problem with just one single role instead.

One role, one filter expression, adapting automatically to whoever happens to actually be signed in at that moment — matched directly against a small user-mapping table you add right into the model yourself, pairing each person's email with what they're specifically allowed to see.

Here's the genuinely classic bug that trips almost everyone up at least once: USERNAME and USERPRINCIPALNAME return noticeably different formats in Desktop compared to the actual live service. Your user-mapping table absolutely has to match the format the service itself actually returns, not necessarily whatever format you happened to see while testing locally in Desktop.

Test as role validates that filter logic directly, without needing a second real person involved at all. Select it from the role's own More options menu — you'll get redirected straight to the underlying report itself, since dashboards genuinely can't be tested this particular way.

Now viewing as lets you test a single role, a combination of several roles together, or even impersonate one specific named person's exact permissions. But remember the real catch here: it still evaluates that dynamic function using your own identity the whole time, never the identity of whoever you're actually trying to simulate.

That's the entire dynamic pattern working correctly, start to finish, from a single role all the way through to a validated filter. Lesson 83 covers exactly what happens once RLS meets a genuinely complex real-world model — bidirectional relationships, and everything that comes along with them.
